summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paradoxical vocal fold motion disorder, hypertension due to primary hyperaldosteronism, type 2 diabetes, pseudotumor cerebri, and tobacco use was admitted for worsening dysphonia over three days, likely exacerbated by household chemical exposure and ongoing smoking. She had no airway compromise or respiratory distress. A neck X-ray showed no obstruction, and her oxygenation remained stable. She was managed conservatively with continued omeprazole for laryngeal reflux and as-needed bronchodilators. Her enalapril was increased to 10 mg daily for improved blood pressure control, and glyburide was doubled to 5 mg daily. She was cleared by her laryngologist for discharge with a same-day outpatient bronchoscopy planned to evaluate for subglottic stenosis. She was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and follow-up instructions.
